Based on the search results you provided, the best open-ear earbuds for running depend on whether you prioritize sound quality, staying aware of traffic, long battery life, or price. My top recommendation for a practical running-focused option is the Soundcore AeroFit 2, while Runner’s World names the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds its overall winner and the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 its top bone-conduction pick.

Best open-ear earbuds for running
Best practical value
1. Soundcore AeroFit 2
$79.99–$129.99

The best all-around value for runners who want ear hooks, environmental awareness, and long battery life. Features include IP55 water resistance, 10 hours per charge, and 42 hours with the case. The supplied results list a promotional code price of $104, subject to eligibility.

Source: Dealectric · SoundGuys

Buy the AeroFit 2

Best overall
2. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds
$199 in the supplied results

A clip-on design that leaves the ear canal open, with excellent audio quality, comfortable wear, and convenient controls. Runner’s World ranks these best overall. The main drawbacks are price and occasional Immersive Audio glitches.

Source: Runner’s World · RTINGS comparison

Buy at Amazon · Buy at Walmart

Best for road running
3. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
$125–$180 in the supplied results

A secure neckband-style design combining bone and air conduction. It leaves your ear canals unblocked, offers IP55 sweat resistance, and is particularly suited to runners who want to hear surrounding traffic without earbuds sitting inside their ears.

Source: WIRED review · RTINGS comparison

Buy at Amazon · Buy at REI

4. JLab Flex Open Earbuds

Best budget alternative

Runner’s World names these its budget pick. They are worth considering if you want an open-ear design without paying premium prices. The supplied results don't include a verified current price or detailed battery specifications.

Source: Runner’s World

Shop JLab Flex Open on Amazon

5. Shokz OpenDots 2

Best for long runs

Runner’s World highlights these for long runs. WIRED reports up to 10 hours of battery life per charge, 40 hours with the case, and IP57 dust and water resistance. Their clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats.

Source: Runner’s World · WIRED

My recommendation

Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2 — a strong mix of battery life, water resistance, and price.

Best premium earbuds: Bose Ultra Open — choose these if sound quality and clip-on comfort matter most.

Best for serious outdoor runners: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 — especially if you prefer bone conduction and a secure neckband.

One important note: open-ear headphones help you hear traffic, but they don't guarantee safety. Keep the volume low enough to hear cyclists, cars, and other runners.
